decisions.rationale: No Mega on my team; opponent's only Mega is Blastoise-Mega. Lead Grimmsnarl+Staraptor: Fake Out flinches Scarf Manectric turn 1, Staraptor Focus Sash guarantees survival to Final Gambit KO Manectric next turn. Intimidate weakens Sneasler; Prankster Taunt stops Sinistcha TR. Back Politoed+Archaludon rain core sweeps once LightningRod is gone. If opponent benches Manectric, Archaludon is immediately free to dominate.
decisions.notebook: G1 confirmed: Manectric Scarf Timid LightningRod—outspeeds all my mons including Noivern 192, Thunderbolt spam, Choice-locked. Pelipper Modest DampRock Drizzle—double-targets Staraptor with Ice Beam. Houndoom Timid Sitrus FlashFire 126-161 spe—Fire Blast can miss. Sneasler Adamant Unburden White Herb 140-172 spe—Unburden doubles speed after White Herb consumption from Close Combat. Opponent rain mirrors mine; LightningRod Manectric hard-counters Archaludon Electro Shot. No player Mega vs opponent Blastoise-Mega available (Mega Launcher boosts Aura Sphere/Dark Pulse). G2 plan: Lead Grimmsnarl+Staraptor to remove Manectric via Fake Out flinch + Final Gambit. If Manectric absent, Archaludon+Politoed rain core free. Grimmsnarl Prankster Taunt stops Sinistcha TR (priority +1 vs TR priority -7). Staraptor Brave Bird 2x SE on Sneasler. Close Combat NVE on Pelipper (0.5x). Key: remove Manectric before committing Archaludon. If opponent expects Final Gambit and Protects Manectric, Staraptor survives (Sash) and retries; Grimmsnarl sets screens or Taunts partner. Watch for Houndoom Taunt on Grimmsnarl—Dark-type immune to Prankster Taunt.

decisions.rationale: Lead Pelipper+Manectric to win weather war (Pelipper Drizzle) and provide Scarf speed control (258 Spe outspeeds Noivern 192). Manectric Lightning Rod absorbs Archaludon Electro Shot. Back Sneasler+Blastoise-Mega: Sneasler Close Combat SE on Archaludon/Garganacl, Unburden boost after White Herb; Blastoise-Mega Launcher boosts Aura Sphere to 120 BP for Steel types. Covers all opponent modes.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 plan: Lead Pelipper+Manectric for weather war + Scarf speed control. Back Sneasler+Blastoise-Mega for Archaludon/Staraptor coverage. Opponent durable tendencies: Grimmsnarl spams Taunt (6 uses G1, full PP reset G2); Archaludon stacks Stamina; Staraptor is physical cleanup with Intimidate. Strategic facts: Screens last 8 turns Light Clay; Noivern Infiltrator bypasses screens; Garganacl Purifying Salt immune to status. Future plans: If opponent leads Politoed+Grimmsnarl, Manectric Volt Switch into Sneasler for Close Combat on Archaludon switch; keep Manectric for Noivern speed tie; Taunt Grimmsnarl with Houndoom if it comes back. Blastoise-Mega timing: bring in after weather/screens settled, Aura Sphere for Archaludon/Garganacl.

decisions.rationale: Manectric Choice Scarf means it can't Protect without locking into Protect permanently, so it must attack or switch. Fake Out (+3 pri) flinches Manectric regardless. Final Gambit KOs (Staraptor 162 HP > Manectric ~147 HP, Fighting neutral on Electric). Staraptor faints before Pelipper moves, so Ice Beam whiffs. Best possible trade: remove the Archaludon hard-counter for Staraptor.
decisions.notebook: G2 T1: Confirmed Manectric Scarf cannot Protect turn 1 without self-locking. Staraptor HP 162 > Manectric HP ~147, Final Gambit neutral on Electric = guaranteed KO if it connects. Choice Scarf Protect self-trap is a known constraint. If opponent hard-switches Manectric to Sinistcha, Final Gambit is immune (Ghost) but Fake Out still flinches. Post-trade plan: bring Archaludon+Politoed rain core vs remaining Pelipper/Houndoom/Sneasler/Blastoise/Sinistcha. Grimmsnarl Prankster Taunt still stops Sinistcha TR. Watch Houndoom Taunt (Dark immune to Prankster). Archaludon Electro Shot useless vs LightningRod if Manectric somehow survives.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon is the clear bring. Electro Shot guaranteed OHKOs Pelipper (4x SE, outspeeds 123 vs 85-117). Manectric/LightningRod is gone so Electro Shot is now live. Steel/Dragon resists Water (Blastoise), quad-resists Grass (Sinistcha), and Fire Blast is rain-weakened (Houndoom). Only Sneasler threatens with a non-guaranteed Close Combat KO. Grimmsnarl can set Reflect next turn to mitigate.
decisions.notebook: G2: Archaludon Electro Shot guaranteed OHKOs Pelipper (4x SE, 140-409%). Sneasler Close Combat possible but not guaranteed OHKO on Archaludon (57-146%). Archaludon outspeeds Pelipper (123 vs 85-117). Houndoom Dark-type blocks Prankster Taunt. Post-Manectric trade: Archaludon+Politoed rain core is the win condition. Grimmsnarl should prioritize Reflect if Sneasler appears, Taunt if Sinistcha appears (TR stop). Watch for Houndoom Taunt outspeeding Grimmsnarl (126-161 vs 86).

decisions.rationale: Double SE special moves on Staraptor. Manectric Thunderbolt 68-165% and Pelipper Ice Beam 46-112% both break Focus Sash; if both land Staraptor dies, if Grimmsnarl flinches one the other still breaks sash leaving Staraptor at 1 HP. Special moves ignore potential Reflect. Manectric Scarf outspeeds Staraptor 258 vs 132-167. Ice Beam over Hydro Pump: 180 effective BP vs 165, plus perfect accuracy. Thunderbolt over Volt Switch: 180 vs 140 effective BP and keeps Manectric in for continued speed contr

Sneasler at 172 Spe outspeeds Grimmsnarl (80-112) and threatens the most likely switch-ins: Close Combat 2x SE on Archaludon (Steel/Dragon) and Rock Slide 2x SE on Noivern (Flying/Dragon). Unburden+WhiteHerb gives a late-game speed surge after a stat-drop move. Blastoise is slower (130) and walled by Garganacl; Sneasler hits Rock 2x SE. Pelipper Pass avoids feeding Grimmsnarl a free Taunt on Protect and keeps rain up for Sneasler's switches.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 update: Manectric fainted T1 to Staraptor Final Gambit + Grimmsnarl Fake Out flinch. Pivot to Sneasler as Archaludon counter; reserve Blastoise-Mega for late rain abuse after screens/weather settle. Opponent durable tendencies: Grimmsnarl spams Taunt + screens (Light Clay 8 turns); Archaludon stacks Stamina; Garganacl Purifying Salt immune to status. Strategic facts: Noivern Infiltrator bypasses screens; Politoed Drizzle overwrites rain. Future plans: If Politoed switches in, Sneasler Close Combat chunks before it sets rain; if Archaludon comes, Sneasler Close Combat 2x SE; if Noivern comes, Sneasler Rock Slide 2x SE; bring Blastoise-Mega after one screen is broken or vs Garganacl for Aura Sphere.

decisions.rationale: Prankster Reflect (+1 priority) lands before Sneasler attacks, halving Close Combat to survivable range (~32-66%). Archaludon then outspeeds and KO's Pelipper with 4x SE Electro Shot. Even if Pelipper Protects, Reflect is still valuable and opponent wasted their turn. Taunt line risks Archaludon OHKO without Reflect.
decisions.notebook: G2: Archaludon Electro Shot guaranteed OHKOs Pelipper (4x SE, 140-409%). Sneasler Close Combat possible but not guaranteed OHKO on Archaludon (57-146%). Archaludon outspeeds Pelipper (123 vs 85-117). Houndoom Dark-type blocks Prankster Taunt. Post-Manectric trade: Archaludon+Politoed rain core is the win condition. Grimmsnarl should prioritize Reflect if Sneasler appears, Taunt if Sinistcha appears (TR stop). Watch for Houndoom Taunt outspeeding Grimmsnarl (126-161 vs 86). Sneasler has Unburden+WhiteHerb: after Close Combat it consumes White Herb and doubles Speed, becoming extremely fast for rest of game. Reflect halves physical damage making Close Combat survivable on Archaludon (~32-66%). Poison Jab on Grimmsnarl with Reflect still possible KO on high roll (32-74% vs 73% HP).

decisions.rationale: Double-target Archaludon to remove Electro Shot threat. Sneasler CC 2x SE likely OHKOs (62.9-109.1%); Pelipper Ice Beam neutral (Ice vs Steel/Dragon = 1x) adds 23.9-46.7% as insurance. Even if Grimmsnarl Fakes Out Sneasler, Pelipper still chunks Archaludon to ~53-76% HP, finishable next turn. Sneasler White Herb cures CC drops, Unburden boosts Spe for next turn. Archaludon is the win-con threat; Grimmsnarl at 72% is secondary.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Manectric fainted T1 to Staraptor Final Gambit + Grimmsnarl Fake Out. Sneasler is Archaludon counter (CC 2x SE). Blastoise-Mega reserved for late rain abuse or vs Garganacl (Aura Sphere). Opponent durable tendencies: Grimmsnarl spams Taunt + screens (Light Clay 8 turns); Archaludon stacks Stamina; Garganacl Purifying Salt immune to status. Noivern Infiltrator bypasses screens. Future plans: If Politoed switches in, Sneasler CC chunks before rain overwrite; if Noivern comes, Sneasler Rock Slide 2x SE; bring Blastoise-Mega after screen breaks or vs Garganacl.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Grimmsnarl at 16% and 86 Spe is dead before it acts. Switch to Politoed brings fresh rain setter at 100%. Archaludon Protect avoids the double-target KO (Close Combat 37-65% with Reflect + Mega Aura Sphere 61-115% = likely dead) and denies Sneasler's Unburden since Close Combat whiffs on Protect. Next turn Politoed+Archaludon at 90% with +1 SpA vs 2 foes is a winning position. Electro Shot isn't guaranteed OHKO (78% floor) so attacking risks losing the wincon for nothing.
decisions.notebook: G2: Opponent has only Sneasler+Blastoise remaining (Pelipper+Manectric fainted). Blastoise Blastoisinite Mega Evo: Mega Launcher boosts Aura Sphere/Dark Pulse 1.5x. Sneasler Unburden+WhiteHerb not yet triggered (only used Poison Jab). Archaludon Electro Shot vs Blastoise: 78-170% range, not guaranteed OHKO. With Reflect, Sneasler Close Combat on Archaludon ~37-65%. Mega Launcher Aura Sphere on Archaludon ~61-115%. Blastoise base 78 Spe both forms (98-130 range). Win condition: preserve Archaludon, wear down with Politoed rain support, Electro Shot Blastoise when safe. Grimmsnarl at 16% is emergency screens/Taunt only.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler CC 2x SE on Archaludon OHKOs at 90% (165 Atk vs ~130 Def). Removes rain-boosted Electro Shot threat to Blastoise. Blastoise Hydro Pump in rain (165 effective BP) OHKOs 16% Grimmsnarl neutral. No Mega - save stone for Garganacl Aura Sphere per plan. If Archaludon Protects, WhiteHerb restores Sneasler; next turn CC finishes.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Manectric lost T1 to Staraptor Final Gambit + Grimmsnarl Fake Out. Pelipper lost T2 to Archaludon Electro Shot. Sneasler is Archaludon counter (CC 2x SE). Blastoise-Mega reserved for late rain or vs Garganacl (Aura Sphere 2x SE). Opponent durable tendencies: Grimmsnarl spams Taunt + screens (Light Clay 8 turns); Archaludon stacks Stamina; Garganacl Purifying Salt immune to status. Noivern Infiltrator bypasses screens. Future plans: If Politoed switches in, Sneasler CC chunks before rain overwrite; if Noivern comes, Sneasler Rock Slide 2x SE; bring Blastoise-Mega after screen breaks or vs Garganacl.

decisions.rationale: Opponent has only 2 Pokemon left; both at 100%. Hydro Pump chunks/KOs Sneasler (49-110%), Electro Shot chunks/KOs Blastoise (60-131%). If both faint we win game 2 immediately. Reflect halves Close Combat so Archaludon likely survives Sneasler's hit at 90%. Hydro Pump 80% acc is the main risk but upside of instant win justifies it. Ice Beam too weak (18-40%) to meaningfully damage Sneasler.
decisions.notebook: G2: Opponent remaining: Sneasler+Blastoise only (Pelipper+Manectric fainted). Blastoise Blastoisinite unevolved through turn 4. Sneasler White Herb+Unburden NOT yet triggered (Close Combat on t3 was blocked by Protect, no stat drops). If Sneasler lands Close Combat this turn, White Herb consumes, Unburden doubles Speed to ~280-344. Win condition: KO both this turn or preserve Archaludon for Electro Shot on Blastoise. Grimmsnarl 16% emergency only. Series: down 0-1, must win G2.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler CC 2x SE on Archaludon chunks while it can't move (chose no Protect). Blastoise HPump into Politoed threatens KO in rain. Save Mega for later.
decisions.notebook: Mega reserved for late rain or Garganacl. Sneasler = Archaludon counter (CC 2x). Noivern Infiltrator beats screens. Archaludon stacks Stamina; bait it. Grimmsnarl screens 8t, Taunt support.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler is the last foe at 7% and outspeeds both my mons. Archaludon Protect blocks the SE Close Combat KO; Politoed's Ice Beam (100% acc, 90 BP neutral) easily KOs 7% Sneasler. If Sneasler Protects, we repeat next turn — it can't escape a 2v1. Guaranteed win this turn unless Sneasler Protects, in which case we win next turn.

Sneasler at 8% HP cannot survive any hit this turn. Close Combat into Archaludon (2x SE, 120 BP STAB) KOs Archaludon at 17% HP even after Reflect and +1 Def reduction. This denies opponent Archaludon. Rock Slide does negligible damage (0.5x + Reflect + spread). Protect blocks one hit but Sneasler still faints. Maximize impact by removing Archaludon.

reflections.summary: Won because Staraptor's Final Gambit removed Manectric turn 1, eliminating the opponent's speed control and Lightning Rod threat. Archaludon then swept the rain-weak core (Pelipper and Blastoise both 4x or 2x weak to Electro Shot) under rain, accumulating +2 SpA. The team-preview plan was well-suited: Politoed+Archaludon rain core matched up excellently against the opponent's own rain team, and Grimmsnarl+Staraptor provided the disruption needed to buy Archaludon setup turns.
reflections.adjustment: For game 3, expect the opponent to adjust their bring — Houndoom (Flash Fire) directly walls Archaludon's Electro Shot and Sinistcha (Trick Room) could reverse the speed tier entirely. Consider whether Archaludon remains the best Mega if Houndoom comes, and prepare a Draco Meteor or Flash Cannon contingency. Also avoid trading Staraptor as early if the opponent leads differently; Final Gambit value depends on removing the right target.
reflections.notebook: Opponent roster: Pelipper (Drizzle/DampRock), Sneasler (Unburden/White Herb, Close Combat spam), Manectric (Choice Scarf/LightningRod), Blastoise (Blastoisinite/Torrent), Houndoom (Flash Fire/SitrusBerry — not brought G2), Sinistcha (Trick Room/Leftovers — not brought G2). Opponent favors rain core with Manectric speed control. Sneasler relies on Close Combat to trigger White Herb+Unburden speed doubling; if blocked by Protect, it stays slow. Blastoise Mega evolution was delayed through turn 4 in G2. Opponent may bring Houndoom or Sinistcha in G3 to counter Archaludon rain sweep. Series tied 1-1; game 3 is decisive.

reflections.summary: Lost primarily because the team-preview plan was wrong for this matchup. Manectric (Choice Scarf) was the obvious Fake Out + Final Gambit target and was deleted on turn 1, removing all speed control. Pelipper was then OHKO'd by Archaludon's rain-boosted Electro Shot, stripping rain before Blastoise could capitalize. Blastoise was brought as the Mega but never Mega Evolved across 5 turns, wasting the team's central win condition. Sneasler, the supposed Archaludon counter, was repeatedly blocked b
reflections.adjustment: For game 3, do not bring Manectric into a team with Grimmsnarl + Staraptor — that pairing is a hard counter. Bring Noivern (Infiltrator bypasses Reflect, Hurricane in rain threatens Archaludon/Politoed) and Mega Evolve Blastoise on turn 1 the moment it enters, so rain-boosted Hydro Pump can pressure Politoed before Archaludon sets up. If Archaludon is brought again, lead Sneasler + Pelipper and commit to breaking it turn 2 with Close Combat before it gets a second Stamina stack; do not let it Pr
reflections.notebook: Opponent runs rain (Politoed) with Archaludon (Stamina, Life Orb) as the win condition and Grimmsnarl (Light Clay, Prankster) for Reflect/Light Screen support. Staraptor carries Final Gambit and pairs with Grimmsnarl Fake Out to delete one opposing Pokemon on turn 1 — treat this combo as a hard removal threat when previewing. Archaludon uses Protect aggressively to stack Stamina boosts and is very difficult to OHKO even with super-effective Close Combat; need multiple hits or a different answer (Noivern Hurricane in rain, or Garganacl Salt Cure if they drop Archaludon). Reflect was set turn 2 and lasted the whole game — physical attackers need Infiltrator or screen-breaking support. Blastoise Mega must Mega Evolve immediately on entry; do not sit on the item. Manectric is unsafe vs Fake Out users and should only be brought when Staraptor/Grimmsnarl are absent. Future plan: if opponent keeps this core, lead Pelipper + Sneasler, bring Noivern as the screen-bypasser, and Mega Evolve Blastoise the turn it enters to threaten Politoed before Archaludon stabilizes.
